sources.title: John Milnor, “On Manifolds Homeomorphic to the 7-Sphere,” Annals of Mathematics 64 (1956), pp. 399–405
sources.locator: Visually inspected all seven mathematical pages, printed pp. 399–405 (full eight-page scan includes cover); §3 pp. 402–403 for clutching, characteristic classes and Milnor examples; pp. 399–401 for the lambda invariant and gluing.
sources.read_verification: Per the source audit memo, the full scan was downloaded and all mathematical pages visually inspected. The scan has no usable text layer. This coverage records the audit memo’s inspection; it does not claim that this evidence writer independently downloaded or read the source.

contents.name: Quaternionic clutching bundles over S⁴
contents.support: Scaffolded definition; state orientation, smoothness, connectedness and category hypotheses explicitly, and keep definitions distinct from the group/existence theorems that require proof.

contents.name: Euler number from the clutching obstruction
contents.support: Local proof obligation: construct a hemisphere section and identify the equatorial obstruction degree with the Euler number in the fixed orientation.

contents.name: Pontryagin calibration of left and right quaternionic clutching
contents.support: Local calibration obligation: derive signs using the complex structures/orientations and published Chern/Pontryagin conventions; Milnor’s ± and Northwestern’s projective-space shortcut do not fix/prove the normalization.

contents.name: Degree-four characteristic numbers add under clutching product
contents.support: Local proof obligation: prove additivity under the S4 pinch/group-sum construction, then combine with the two basic clutching calculations.

contents.name: Euler and first Pontryagin classes of ξ_{h,j}
contents.support: Depends on the local Euler-degree and characteristic-number calibrations; prove the fixed convention e=(h+j)u and p1=2(h−j)u.

contents.name: Milnor sphere and disk bundles
contents.support: Scaffolded definition; state orientation, smoothness, connectedness and category hypotheses explicitly, and keep definitions distinct from the group/existence theorems that require proof.

contents.name: Euler number ±1 gives an integral homology seven-sphere
contents.support: Compute integral cohomology by Gysin and use UCT/duality or homology Gysin to rule out torsion.

contents.name: Milnor sphere bundles are simply connected
contents.support: Use the S3→M→S4 fibration LES and simple connectivity of base and fiber.

contents.name: Milnor Euler ±1 bundles are homotopy seven-spheres
contents.support: Supply finite CW models; use Hurewicz to get a generator map S7→M and Whitehead after the integral homology calculation. Exact homology-Whitehead supplier uses actual finite CW models furnished by the new local ACω finite-parameter Morse construction; all choice assumptions are stated.

contents.name: Relative middle form and signature for an eight-manifold with boundary
contents.support: Locally define the relative middle form/image quotient; a closed-manifold signature supplier alone does not define it for a manifold with boundary.

contents.name: Disk-bundle middle form and signature
contents.support: Apply zero-section self-intersection=Euler in the disk-bundle interior and justify its relative boundary-form identification; distinguish e=0 degenerate case from e=±1.

contents.name: Relative square equals mixed evaluation
contents.support: Prove the relative cup-product/cochain identity; the boundary square is not an absolute degree-eight evaluation.

contents.name: Relative Pontryagin square of a Milnor disk bundle
contents.support: Prove tangent splitting, j(U)=εx and normalization <U·x,[W,M]>=1; integer lift formula applies for ε=±1.

contents.name: Milnor lambda candidate from a supplied filling
contents.support: Contract correct hypothesis to H3(M;Z)=H4(M;Z)=0 replaced by integral cohomology H3=H4=0; existence of a supplied filling is conditional, and no independence is asserted by definition.

contents.name: Milnor lambda is an oriented boundary invariant modulo seven
contents.support: Depends on still-open relative-square and signature gluing lemmas; apply the closed 8D signature formula only after gluing N, then reduce 45≡3 mod 7.

contents.name: Milnor’s exotic seven-sphere
contents.support: Depends on the local clutching, homotopy/homeomorphism bridges and lambda gluing proof; concrete (2,−1) gives λ=1 versus standard λ=0.

contents.name: The quaternionic Hopf sphere bundle
contents.support: Give explicit bundle identification with S7 and rely on calibrated e,p1 and lambda proofs; naming Hopf alone does not fix clutching convention. Current dependencies explicitly include the relative-number, disk-signature and lambda theorem used for lambda=0.

contents.name: Gysin calculation of a Milnor homology sphere
contents.support: Specialize integral Gysin to Euler class u and show all intermediate groups vanish.

contents.name: Intersection matrix of a Milnor bound
contents.support: Derive the [1] form from the zero-section Euler self-intersection and boundary relative-form comparison.

contents.name: Two distinct Milnor lambda values
contents.support: Depends on completed lambda calculation; distinguish k=1 and k=3 modulo seven.

contents.name: Topological type does not determine smooth type
contents.support: Follows from the explicit homeomorphism bridge plus the nonzero oriented lambda obstruction (also excludes orientation reversal against zero).

sources.title: M. Kervaire and J. Milnor, “Groups of Homotopy Spheres: I,” Annals of Mathematics 77 (1963), pp. 504–537
sources.locator: Visually inspected printed pp. 504–515 only, covering §§1–4 and start of §5; theorem 3.1 pp. 508–509; order-28 statement/table p. 512. Later §§7–8 were not inspected; p. 512 is not a local derivation.
sources.read_verification: The audit memo reports fetching the complete scan and visually inspecting pp. 504–515. This evidence writer relies on that memo and makes no independent source-reading claim.

contents.support: Scaffolded definition; state orientation, smoothness, connectedness and category hypotheses explicitly, and keep definitions distinct from the group/existence theorems that require proof.

contents.name: Connected sum descends to oriented h-cobordism classes
contents.support: Local proof obligation: connected-sum well-definedness under oriented h-cobordism, using disk embeddings/isotopy extension and collars; KM Lemma 2.1 imports Cerf/Palais facts. Exact homology-Whitehead supplier uses actual finite CW models furnished by the new local ACω finite-parameter Morse construction; all choice assumptions are stated.

contents.name: Orientation reversal is the connected-sum inverse
contents.support: Local proof obligation: construct the inverse h-cobordism via the contractible-bound construction of KM Lemma 2.4; do not assume arbitrary disk complements contractible. Exact homology-Whitehead supplier uses actual finite CW models furnished by the new local ACω finite-parameter Morse construction; all choice assumptions are stated.

contents.name: The homotopy-sphere group Θ_n
contents.support: Definition only; associativity, commutativity, identity and inverse must be justified by distinct local lemmas.

contents.name: H-cobordism of homotopy spheres equals oriented diffeomorphism
contents.support: Local Θ proof obligation: justify connected-sum operation on oriented h-cobordism classes and match the h-cobordism dimension n+1≥6 hypotheses; the definition itself supplies no group axioms.

contents.name: Parallelizable bounds define a subgroup
contents.support: Local proof obligation: representative independence and closure by extending framings over boundary connected sum and reversing orientation.

contents.name: The subgroup bP_{n+1}
contents.support: Scaffolded definition; state orientation, smoothness, connectedness and category hypotheses explicitly, and keep definitions distinct from the group/existence theorems that require proof.

contents.name: Homotopy spheres are stably parallelizable
contents.support: Non-load-bearing not-supplied result. Full proof requires Bott stable pi(SO), Pontryagin obstruction comparison and Adams J-injectivity; AT/MO detector does not supply them.

contents.name: Kervaire–Milnor calculation of Θ₇
contents.support: Non-load-bearing not-supplied result. Full calculation requires stable stems, image of J, framed surgery and Kervaire–Milnor arithmetic; p.512 is a checked statement/table locator only.

contents.name: Scope of the order-28 calculation
contents.support: Scope boundary: states that stable stems, J and Kervaire–Milnor arithmetic are external and non-load-bearing; do not infer the concrete quaternionic construction from the classification.

short_document_reading.publication: J. Francis (notes by Y. Shen), MATH 465 Lecture 18: Milnor's Construction of Exotic 7-Spheres, Second Part, Northwestern University, May 10, 2010
short_document_reading.completeness_evidence: The served PDF is a complete three-page handout; all three pages were downloaded and read in full (mutool text extraction): p.1 recapitulation and lambda setup; pp.1-2 Proposition 2.2 and its gluing proof with the Omega^SO_7=0 statement; pp.2-3 the lambda computation, Lemma 3.1, Lemma 3.2 and the M_k^7 conclusion. Prop. 2.1's proof is left blank in the source, and the two printed slips (orientation-reversal shorthand and the HP^2 denominator 1+3x) are recorded out-of-scope in this coverage.

source_resolution.reason: Fetch-stamp blocked by the short-document completeness rule, not by unavailability: the served body is a complete three-page handout and was downloaded and read in full (the short_document_reading receipt is retained on this entry), but source-fetch-check's six-attempt budget was consumed in one invocation by six identical 'missing full-document reading receipt' classifications recorded before the reading receipt was entered, so this URL can no longer receive the mechanical stamp. The lecture supports no included result: its only two recorded contents are out-of-scope printed slips (the orientation-reversal shorthand and the 1+3x HP^2 denominator). Every result of the pair is backed by the three fetch-verified treatments (Milnor 1956; Kervaire-Milnor 1963; Milnor's h-cobordism lectures) and the local support items, and an independent complete treatment of the same construction was located (McEnroe, UChicago REU 2015). sources.title: John Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem, §9
sources.locator: §9 Proposition B and corollary, printed pp. 109–110: two-disk complement, twisted sphere, and Alexander extension.
sources.read_verification: The audit memo reports checking the OCR text of the specified pages in the complete 121-page scan and separately reading the current batch-15 supplier statement. No broader reading of this book is claimed here.

contents.name: Two-disk complement is an h-cobordism
contents.support: Prove each boundary inclusion is a homotopy equivalence (relative homology/excision, van Kampen, finite-CW Whitehead); cobordism dimension d≥6. Exact homology-Whitehead supplier uses actual finite CW models furnished by the new local ACω finite-parameter Morse construction; all choice assumptions are stated.

contents.name: Alexander extension over a disk
contents.support: Write the radial extension and verify continuity at the center and its inverse; it is topological, not generally smooth there.

contents.name: Milnor homotopy seven-spheres are topological spheres
contents.support: Source identifies the claim and its scope; complete the local argument with the stated hypotheses and the available published/same-run supplier interfaces. Source availability is not proof closure.

contents.name: The smooth four-dimensional boundary
contents.support: Source identifies the claim and its scope; complete the local argument with the stated hypotheses and the available published/same-run supplier interfaces. Source availability is not proof closure.

canonical.name: Boundary middle-form nondegeneracy and signature gluing
canonical.support: Local repair: define the compact-boundary signature using the relative middle form, prove nondegeneracy from Poincare–Lefschetz duality, and establish the gluing comparison. The cited lecture is not used as proof.

canonical.name: Relative Pontryagin squares glue across a seven-dimensional boundary
canonical.support: Local repair: use collars, relative excision, Mayer–Vietoris and relative cup products to identify the two filling evaluations with the closed Pontryagin number; this is proved in the separate research memo, not attributed to the Northwestern lecture.

canonical.name: Relative Kronecker evaluation is well defined and natural
canonical.support: Local interface proof from relative cochains and chains, including independence from representatives and naturality; the source audit maps it to published relative-cohomology suppliers.

canonical.name: Relative degree-four cup products are symmetric
canonical.support: Local proof descends the natural diagonal chain homotopy to relative cochains; it closes the symmetry interface used for the boundary middle form.

canonical.name: Relative cap product matches relative evaluation
canonical.support: Local front-face/back-face cochain identity and the relative cap boundary formula supply the evaluation step needed for Poincare–Lefschetz duality.

canonical.name: Collared gluing supplies relative excision and evaluation maps
canonical.support: Local collar cover and excision proof identifies the two relative filling pairs and their fundamental-class evaluations without extending arbitrary singular cocycles by zero.

canonical.name: Compact oriented boundary manifolds have finite-dimensional cohomology
canonical.support: Local double-and-retract argument plus the published finite-generation and field-UCT suppliers gives the finite-dimensionality required by the boundary-form definition.

canonical.name: Integral middle-cohomology vanishing implies real vanishing
canonical.support: Local UCT argument checks the coefficient change for the relative gluing comparison; finite generation and divisibility of R remove the Hom and Ext terms.

canonical.name: The disk-bundle Thom class pairs with the base generator
canonical.support: Local double, zero-section Thom/PD supplier and collar evaluation comparison prove the sign-normalized relative pairing used in q(W).

canonical.name: The Milnor disk bundle tangent bundle has the required stable splitting
canonical.support: Local vertical tangent sequence, connection splitting and TS4 plus a trivial line identify p1(TW) with the stated clutching-bundle class.

canonical.name: Compact smooth manifolds have finite CW models under countable choice
canonical.support: Local finite-parameter Morse/Sard construction under ACω, followed by finite handle-to-cell models; avoids unsupported compactness-to-finite-CW inference and preserves the Theta/bP choice boundary. Full proof body remains a Step3 obligation.
